a significant fraction of Ca2+ uptake by mitochondria depends on TRPC3, a Ca2+-permeable channel that is localized to the mitochondrial outer membrane.
a fraction of TRPC3 is localized to mitochondrion and contributes to mitochondrial Ca2+, and the up- or down-regulation of its expression in cells influences the mitochondrial membrane potentials.
a fraction of TRPC3 channels is localized to the mitochondria, and that TRPC3 is involved in regulation of mitochondrial calcium uptake.

the molecular identity of mitochondrial Ca2+, the mechanisms of mitochondrial calcium uptake and the physiological roles of TRPC3 channels.
the role of Ca2+ channels in mitochondria, and in particular, the contribution of TRPC3 channels to mitochondrial Ca2+.
the role of TRPC channels in the mitochondria and how this may affect mitochondrial function.

TRPC3 is a mitochondrial calcium uptake channel and that TRPC3 expression influences the mitochondrial membrane.

a fraction of the canonical transient receptor potential channel 3 (TRCP3) channels is present on mitochondria and that these channels are important for the mitochondrial Ca2+ influx.
